matches.quote: The RB-mixed state therefore persists only while non-zero gate voltages are held inside the bistable window, which is weaker than the usual meaning of non-volatility in memory
Fig. 3a overlays blue contours from a different contact configuration on data from the main configuration. Mark them clearly or show them on a separate map
The caption assigns the −4.1 and −15.5×10^12 cm^-2 thresholds to the "forward and backward scans, respectively"... Check that both agree with the legend arrows.
Reproducibility across devices and contacts is unclear... In device A the switching occurs only in part of the device (Extended Data Fig. 4)
image a device after setting it into each state, with spatially resolved Raman (the 2D-band lineshape distinguishes ABAB, ABCA and ABCB), KPFM or nano-IR/near-field imaging.
Nothing shows that ΔU is in fact constant along each experimental contour... plot the calculated ΔU along each experimental contour with its spread
The stacking identity of the domains in device A... is not established... The 22 mV KPFM contrast... is of the order expected for polar-domain contrast.
The 22 mV ΔΦ enters the calculation directly, but it was measured... on a sample on SiO2 or on a stamp. Give the measurement conditions... and the uncertainty
All main-text data come from device A... The text does not say whether device B shows the gate-driven structural switching... and the on/off AHE.
As it stands, the data are also consistent with purely electronic bistability in a fixed domain landscape, for example hysteresis between competing correlated states
"First-order quantum phase transition" (p. 2) is not accurate for a hysteretic structural transition... "Gate-driven first-order structural transition" would be more accurate.
If a modest rhombohedral area fraction gives an AHE larger than that of a pure rhombohedral device, the measured R_yx is not a simple area average
test whether the sign reversal occurs exactly at D = 0 or is offset, that is, whether the sign follows D or the layer that holds the carriers
show: - the switching thresholds and hysteresis width versus temperature, at least up to and above ~8 K and ideally to tens of kelvin

notes: The review was written from the main-text v1 without Extended Data Figs. 1-11 or the SI (noted in P18). As a result, concerns about specific panels in the Extended Data or SI (C6, C10, C11, C16) could only be raised partly or not at all, although for C2 the reviewer correctly deduced from the main text that device B was not shown to exhibit the on/off AHE switching. For C9, P23 challenges whether the calculated energy difference is actually constant along the experimental contours in Fig. 3b without singling out the high negative density corner, so it is graded 'partly'. For C15, P16 (polar ABAC/ABCB 3+1 layer stacking) and P17 (testing whether the AHE sign tracks the carrier-holding layer) raise closely related layer-asymmetry alternatives, graded 'partly'.
